findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 19 exercise as printed on PDF 56-58 (printed pages 53-55), in the book's words and order.
Counts: Q1 nine MCQs (I-IX, options a-d), Q2 nine short-answer questions (a-i), Q3 four constructed-response questions (a-d), Descriptive Questions Q4-Q7 (four); all solved in English and Roman Urdu.
The book prints no answer key. MCQ keys worked out: I d, II b, III c, IV c, V b, VI b, VII d, VIII c, IX b.

Book corrections (kept as printed, Book correction box after the item): Short a asks for enantiomers of 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which is achiral (answered for 2-methylbutan-1-ol); Q7 asks for a meso form of lactic acid, which has one chiral carbon (no meso form). MCQ VI is keyed b (C-2 by IUPAC numbering, 4-methylpentan-2-ol), not boxed (owner rule 2026-11-13: only serious, 100% verified errors are boxed). MCQ III option d 'substation' and Short a 'enantioers' fixed silently.

Doubtful: MCQ IV (urea) keyed c amide; 'all of these' could be argued since urea contains C=O and NH2 parts. MCQ I keyed d CCl4 (chapter lists CO2, CO, carbonates and cyanides as inorganic; CS2 treated as inorganic by convention, not stated in the chapter).

Printed structures of Short c are drawn (2026-11-11) after the question: (a) cyclohexane ring, (b) five-carbon chain with two double bonds = penta-1,3-diene C5H8, (c) four-membered ring with two double bonds = cyclobutadiene C4H4. Drawing questions (Q3 b-d, Q7) answered in words, no figures. Beyond the chapter: Q3(a) side-chain detail of toluene chlorination (the chapter gives the free radical mechanism for CH4 + Cl2); Q3(c) reasoning for 3-methylhexane (the chapter does not name it). Comparison answers Q4 and Q7 carry two-column answer tables. Draft for the academic review.
